name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Switch to the NVIDIA H100 with the Llama 3.4 70B model. It’s the fastest closed-source option we can run right now, and the 70B size hits the sweet spot between speed and capability for EXCAVA’s workload. The trade-off is cost—H100s are expensive—but the gain in raw throughput justifies it for a 0.5%+ lift.

name: Torque
text: The H100’s speed gain is a red herring if EXCAVA’s bottleneck is data ingestion or model accuracy, not compute. A cheaper, newer open model like Llama 3.3 70B (if accessible) or a distilled variant could deliver the 0.5% lift without the cost or lock-in risk—test both on a 1% slice of live data to settle it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run a 1% slice of live data through both the NVIDIA H100 with Llama 3.4 70B and the latest open Llama 3.3 70B (if accessible) in parallel. The H100 gives us the raw speed to see if compute is the bottleneck, while the open model tests whether a cheaper, newer option can hit the 0.5% lift without the cost or lock-in. If the open model matches or beats the H100’s output, we switch to it; if not, we accept the H100’s higher cost for guaranteed throughput. This kills two birds with one stone—no assumptions, just data.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t just cost or lock-in—it’s that neither model’s accuracy on your live data is known until you test, and a 1% slice may not expose the failure mode. A better alternative: run a 10% slice through both, but first validate model accuracy on a held-out benchmark that matches EXCAVA’s domain—if neither clears the benchmark, the bottleneck isn’t compute. Settle it by measuring lift on the benchmark *and* the 10% slice; if neither hits 0.5%, pivot to a domain-specific fine-tune or data pipeline fix.
